implementation_consequences: L301-326 displays averages with signal-count denominators, bars-to-success with success-count denominators, failure-clamped win/loss ratios, and frequency divided by bar_index. Preserve these distinct denominator definitions; a display ratio is not realized profitability or execution evidence.

L329-366 plots new bullish/bearish events and selectable MA debug lines. Visual arrow timing must be separated from fully available signal state; this chunk does not establish how newBullish/newBearish or future outcome labels are formed.

L30-50 requests previous daily close (close[1]) for chart instrument and selected volatility symbol with gaps_off and lookahead_on. Prior-period offset may permit causal daily alignment, but lookahead setting alone neither proves a leak nor certifies historical publication availability. Preserve source close timestamp, release/receipt and fill-forward age; never treat every intraday row as a new observation.

L58-100 scales volatility separately by 16 and sqrt(365), then uses exp(log(Index) +/- scaled volatility times 0.25/0.5/1/1.5). These are two distinct annualization conventions, with positive and negative boundary ordering deliberately swapped. Require positive Index, finite volatility, declared units/horizon and band ordering; do not claim probabilistic coverage from multiplier names.

implementation_consequences: L45-54 and L88-109 store 48 extrema slot counts and commit the previous session only when a new session starts and both high/low slots exist. Current incomplete session must remain excluded from completed-session distributions; the final session needs explicit finalization policy.

L103 bins by time_close using default hour/minute context. Preserve timezone, bar close convention, valid timeframe and session-break definitions; strict high/low comparisons select the first tied extremum.

L123-140 divides each high/low count by its own summed counts, shows zero when denominator absent, and clears table on invalid timeframe. Runtime support should distinguish no observations from a measured 0% probability; display hiding is not an eligibility contract.

findings.path: /workspace/planning/trading-model/review/pine-extracted/Pinescript-indicators--main/First presented FVG (with stats) with statistical hourly ranges & bias.txt
implementation_consequences: L148-163 requires bull low>high[2] plus close>high[2] (bear mirror), anchors formation at mtfTime[2], and gates by middle candle hour. Drawing starts earlier than three-bar pattern detection; birth/known time must not be backdated to that anchor. MTF bar finality and repeated chart evaluations need explicit deduplication.

L170-248 captures first FVG in separate W1/W2/hour windows, with bull precedence. inW1 boolean OR can include pre-09:30 currentHour==9 while w1WindowClosed is false; preserve literal behavior as a compatibility issue and separately specify intended window bounds. Weekend flags do not establish holiday/early-close coverage.

L254-304 hardcodes 24-hour mean/median range, continuation, FVG effectiveness, bullish bias, and W1/confluence probabilities and counts (including 100% cells). These are frozen historical claims lacking fit cohort/time in this passage, not calibrated live probabilities. Version provenance and reconstruct preceding-only estimates before predictive use.
L424-427 creates symmetric plus/minus hourly-open percentage range. This differs from a signed endpoint distribution or total high-low range allocation and needs definition parity.

L492-629 gates continuation on first15minSet and confluence on W1/W2 closure; preserve Pending versus No FVG. W1 label currently reports No FVG without the W2-style pending branch. timenow countdown is display-only and cannot enter replay state.

L18-68 configures dual moving-average/volatility trend basis, ADX/zscore lookbacks, persistent transition probabilities, adaptive learning and temperature. p_stay inputs have max bounds but no explicit minimum here; runtime must validate stochastic rows and finite parameter domains.

L88-163 combines fast/slow MA basis, smoothed TR/StDev/ATR band, stateful optional min/max ratchet, and ATR-normalized trail position/slope plus rolling ADX zscores. Checkpoint all recursive and rolling warmup state and distinguish insufficient/zero-dispersion observations from the literal zero fallbacks.

L168-248 initializes heuristic Gaussian emissions, multiplies three feature likelihoods under a shared state sigma, floors likelihood at 1e-30, temperature-scales it, and performs forward prediction/update. Preserve update ordering and posterior normalization; consider stable log-domain equivalent only with independent literal parity. Posterior is a model-state probability, not an empirically calibrated trade success probability.

L257-277 learns after the posterior update only when a regime exceeds 0.5, moves means first, then uses mean absolute residual versus the updated means to adjust sig with a floor. This is not a sample standard-deviation estimator; retain exact recurrence and preceding parameter version for predictions. No retrospective smoothing or future-fit parameters.

L282-382 ties collapse to chop; visual smoothing of RGB, confidence thresholds 50/65 and alert transitions are separate from numeric state. A change alert does not establish tradability or execution permission.
L537-573 initializes persistent CISD levels, indices, sweep flags and prior OHLC/time state. Checkpoint exact state and retain discovery time separately from historical candidate anchors.

L603-658 derives candidate opens from candle direction/doji conditions and bounded backwards searches (bear side 2..10 shown), stopping if earlier highs exceed current. Confirmed candidate discovery must not be retroactively assigned to candidate bar_index; exact strict/equal comparisons and tie handling matter.

L660-676 repeats high/low threshold blocks: first sets search flags false then immediately true under the same conditions while resetting counters/CISD flags. Literal sequential overwrite is material; do not merge apparent duplicates or infer intent without a separate definition decision. Missing intervening lines are outside this assigned chunk extent, not independently reread here.

L10-21 declares IB09:30-10:30, ORB configurable minutes and RTH09:30-16:00 America/New_York, with lower-timeframe intrabar source. Calendar version, partial sessions, source coverage and LTF<=chart checks are required; nominal session strings are not proof of complete tape.

L147-211 resets/fills extrema and LTF arrays, seals at session exit, finds first final high/low touch, then classifies range against PRIOR sessions before appending current range. Preserve this fit ordering and publish final-range-derived direction only after the seal.

L191-203 and L213-229 choose high on same-subbar extrema or breakout ties, and fall back to chart OHLC when LTF absent. A faithful literal adapter should retain the rule as declared heuristic, while causal output must preserve unresolved intrabar ordering/coverage rather than claim observed high-first.

L232-300 tallies completed sessions once at RTH exit and stores separate formed-first/broke-first/neither and category counts, plus ORB/IB direction 3x3 matrix. Keep denominators, pending/watching/none distinctions, idempotence and finalization controls; no-break requires covered opportunity interval.

L325-432 exposes category continuation percentage divided by all category sessions, not only breakout sessions. Minimum-sample dimming is display-only; runtime uncertainty/support must be explicit. Hist arrays shown here append without a visible cap and need declared bounded retention.

L15-34 hardcodes ORB5/ORB15/combo and post-IB trade-type direction percentages/sample counts, with nominal knowledge times09:35/09:45/10:30. These are archived statistics requiring dated fit provenance and actual feature availability, not runtime empirical validation.

L236-294 uses close>=mid as Upper, explicit extension/fade combinations and fallback unknown predictions. Keep strict versus inclusive midpoint choices versioned across related scripts; do not assign an IB-derived trade type before final IB extrema/order/close are known.

findings.path: /workspace/planning/trading-model/review/pine-extracted/Pinescript-indicators--main/Initial Balance & Extensions with Stats by DOW.txt
implementation_consequences: L425-560 tracks post-IB extrema and hits against historical mean/median or multiples of delta-history SD, commits extensions at the next IB start, and groups by dayofweek(time[1]). Extension horizon may exceed RTH; day labeling must use explicit session identity rather than the preceding bar calendar day.

L455-495 appends the just-finished extension before computing its zscore. This is self-including descriptive normalization, unlike the preceding-only IB ORB Live Stats classifier. Preserve versioned definition and avoid using a later computed score at the old extension time; guard zero SD.

L432-558 conditions hit measurement on show_extensions/show_sd controls. Presentation settings must not silently change research target counts. Record opportunity denominators and coverage alongside hit-only arrays.

L603-618 runs breakout scan at IB exit using bar_index+i conditions but high[i]/low[i] historical values. The forward-looking index arithmetic does not make these future bars; this is a suspected window/direction defect, requiring an independently specified post-IB event scan before implementation.

L683-698 multiplies observed breakout fraction by (1+abs(negative z)*0.1), without a bound shown. Treat as uncalibrated heuristic that may exceed100%, not probability. L705-837 reports separate per-DOW range, extension, break, hit and total arrays; verify shared denominators and empty cohorts.
L17-18 uses IB08:30-09:30 and tracking09:30-16:00, different from other IB scripts. Do not conflate session definitions by indicator family/name.

L225-241 appends current IB range before zscore, making descriptive normalization self-including. L315-472 anchors completed-session levels/Fibonacci/mean/median/percentile/SD extensions at bar_index[offset]; output known time remains completion time. Percentiles use linear interpolation of break-only extensions, unlike all-session extensions.
L476-514 records broad post-IB extrema at next IB start and computes self-including extension zscores; broad horizon differs from separately tracked break-session extensions.

L534-581 resets on IB end, checks strict high>IBH/low<IBL during break session, and records high/low/both/neither once at session exit. Both does not reveal first-touch order; missing coverage cannot become Neither. Maintain selected-break-only extension denominator and a separate all-session denominator.

L639-646 labels Huge/Small/Medium by distance to historical max/min/average, not a calibrated percentile. L683-688 boosts breakout fraction for negative current z without probability bounds. Runtime must preserve heuristic status, cohort fit cutoff and zero-denominator/dispersion support.

L10-18 uses IB09:30-10:30 and RTH09:30-16:00; L44-75 hardcodes asymmetric percentage extensions and multi-condition probability/sample/retest tables. These source constants need dated fit cohort evidence, and percentage-of-high/low extension units must remain distinct from points or IB-range multiples.

L268-286 tracks both breaks independently and midpoint leave/retest with 0.1% threshold. Endpoint-near-midpoint test is not equivalent to OHLC interval crossing the midpoint; a wide crossing bar can be missed. Need explicit retest geometry, first-touch ambiguity, horizon, and one-time transition policy.

L301-360 seals IB and scans frozen LTF bars for first touches of final extrema, choosing high on same-subbar tie. No valid extreme becomes none, but stored_high_first=(extreme==high) turns none into false; later table selection maps it to the low-first branch despite UI Unknown. Preserve unknown eligibility and avoid this false classification.
L352-354 uses bullish c>=o but above-mid c>m. Exact midpoint/doji boundary conventions differ from related scripts and require versioned fixtures.

L358-360 appends IB range then bounds lookback; L445-448 computes mean/percentile including current range. Final extrema-derived state and these descriptive statistics are only known after seal; backdated drawing coordinates in L395-429 must not alter their birth time.

L454-524 selects and displays archived tables and next-break argmax, with tie fallback Neither. This is a prediction display, not verified predictive quality. Conditional post-break updates need separately timed evidence; later file lines are outside this assigned read.
